title: Pre-Analysis — Fire Handle Standard Offered as a Mandatory Action
abstract: Closed re-analysis of the fire handle standard, run on a proposal to make the retrofit mandatory, which was sent back for re-scoping because the case rests on training rather than on airworthiness.

sections.objective: Assess a proposal to make the fire handle retrofit a mandatory action, following a regulator's interest in the ambiguity between the two discharge positions.
sections.findings_summary: The proposal was sent back. Three items were confirmed. The delivered handle meets its certification basis and the regulator raised no airworthiness finding, so a mandatory action would have to rest on the operational evidence alone, and that evidence is training evidence rather than in-service evidence: four unintended discharges and two omissions in several hundred thousand drills. The analysis judged that insufficient. Second, and more useful, the trouble shooting procedure written for the new handle carries a probability of thirty-two per cent for a failed legend cap, which was estimated rather than measured because the handle is barely in service; making the action mandatory would have put that estimate in front of every operator. Third, the pylon zone is shared with the cowl latch installation and a fleet-wide campaign would have collided with the residual latch work.
sections.next_steps: Re-scope as a recommended action with the training case stated openly. Replace the estimated legend cap probability with measured data after the first hundred embodiments. Coordinate any campaign with the residual cowl latch population.

similarity_seeds: an ambiguity found in training rather than in service

tasks.title: Assess the evidence base for a mandatory action
Check campaign interaction in the pylon

expected_findings.rationale: The procedure carries a thirty-two per cent probability for a failed legend cap, which was estimated rather than measured because the handle is barely in service. A mandatory action would have put that estimate in front of every operator as if it were experience.
expected_findings.resolution: Probability to be replaced with measured data after the first hundred embodiments.

expected_findings.rationale: The residual cowl latch campaign is still running in the same nacelle zone, and a second fleet-wide campaign would have competed for the same line slots on the same aircraft.
expected_findings.resolution: Any future campaign to be sequenced behind the latch closure.

expected_findings.rationale: Making the bulletin mandatory would require an airworthiness directive, and the delivered handle meets its certification basis with no finding raised. The case rests on training evidence, which the analysis judged insufficient for a mandatory action.
expected_findings.resolution: Bulletin retained as recommended with the training case stated openly in the planning information.

type_data.conclusion: Mandatory action rejected and returned for re-scoping. The case is a training case and should be presented as one.
